Part A:
We seek the smallest positive integer $x$ satisfying:
$x \equiv 0 \pmod 5$
$x \equiv 8 \pmod 9$
$x \equiv 4 \pmod{16}$

From $x \equiv 4 \pmod{16}$, we can write $x = 16k + 4$. Substituting into the modulo 9 congruence:
$16k + 4 \equiv 8 \pmod 9 \implies 7k \equiv 4 \pmod 9 \implies k \equiv 7 \pmod 9$.
Thus, $x \equiv 16(7) + 4 = 116 \pmod{144}$.

Substituting $x = 144m + 116$ into the modulo 5 congruence:
$144m + 116 \equiv 0 \pmod 5 \implies -m + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod 5 \implies m \equiv 1 \pmod 5$.
The smallest positive value occurs at $m = 1$:
$x = 144(1) + 116 = 260$.
